cur:objects-berlin-deesis-ivory.summary: Under a pierced canopy Christ stands frontally on a footstool, holding a book and blessing, while the Virgin Mary and St John the Baptist turn toward him with hands raised in supplication. This group, the Deesis ('entreaty'), shows the two greatest saints interceding with Christ for humanity. Its quiet symmetry made it one of the most beloved Byzantine images of prayer.
facts: The Deesis became a central Byzantine theme from the 10th century, appearing on ivories, icons and later on the templon screens of churches (type).

wga:zearly/1/4mosaics/2ravenna/4nuovo/5t.summary: Against a gold ground, a young, beardless Christ in imperial purple stands with arms outstretched between four apostles; with one hand he blesses the loaves held out by the disciple at the left, and with the other the fishes held by the disciple at the right. Calm and frontal, Christ gives rather than performs, and the scene became an image of the Eucharistic bread that he still provides.
facts: It belongs to the cycle of 13 small panels of Christ's miracles and parables along the upper north wall, in which Christ is always young and beardless; on the facing wall, scenes of the Passion show him bearded.
These panels date from the time of Theodoric the Great, whose palace church was dedicated in 504.
The scenes are thought to follow the Gospel readings used in the church during Lent.
wga:zearly/1/4mosaics/2ravenna/4nuovo/5t.notes: WGA title 'Christ between Four Apostles' made more specific; the miracle is identified by WGA itself.
